chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Khalaf al-Qammad, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her), recited every day after every prayer, is more beloved to me than the prayer of a thousand rak'ahs offered every day.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward of reciting Tasbih of Fatimah Zahra after prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the exceptional spiritual weight of the Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her), declaring it more beloved to him than performing a thousand voluntary rak'ahs daily. This comparison underscores the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt's devotions in Shia tradition, linking the intercessory merit of the Prophet's household directly to the believer's daily ritual practice. The emphasis on 'after every prayer' (dubur al-salah) suggests its role as a consistent, accessible means of accumulating reward comparable to extensive independent worship.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3.  It  is  narrated  that  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  said,  “I  like reciting this Tasbih every day after Salaat more than offering a thousand rakats of prayer daily.”
